name: Ebiasaph
overview: Ebiasaph was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as a Kohathite. He is noted in Scripture as the son of Elkanah, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for sacred duties. His designation as a Kohathite highlights his connection to one of the key Levitical families entrusted with the care of the tabernacle.
namesAndTitles: The name Ebiasaph means '[my] father has gathered,' a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:23. This meaning reflects a familial or covenantal gathering, though the name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ebiasaph as the son of Elkanah, with an inferred relationship to Assir as his father. Beyond these connections, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ebiasaph's significance lies primarily in his role within the Levitical priestly line, particularly as a Kohathite, a group charged with important religious responsibilities. His lineage through Elkanah situates him within the sacred heritage that served the Lord's sanctuary. Although briefly mentioned, his inclusion underscores the faithful transmission of Levitical duties across generations.
